---
applyTo: "src/Bff/**,src/Tools/SuperApp.Cli/Templates/superapp-bff/**"
---

# BFF experience (`src/Bff/{Experience}.Bff`)

- A BFF is the only entry point of its experience behind the shared edge gateway (ADR-0038). It is a stateless ASP.NET Core MVC host:
  no database, no `DbContext`, no domain model, no migrations, no references to service projects (not even `{Service}.Contracts`) or to
  another BFF (architecture rules 12–14). Domain services never reference a BFF. A read cache (`HybridCache`) is allowed.
- New BFF: `dotnet superapp add bff {Experience}` (template `src/Tools/SuperApp.Cli/Templates/superapp-bff` and every registration, ADR-0046); a client of a
  service of the experience: `dotnet superapp add client --bff {experience} --service {Service}`. Helm chart `deploy/helm/superapp-bff`. Example:
  `src/Bff/Example.Bff` (facade of Knowledge and SleepDiary plus composed endpoints).
- The BFF orchestrates within its experience and shapes data for the module. Business logic stays in the domain services; one request
  never changes the state of several domains (cross-domain processes are events and sagas).

## Two APIs, two contracts (ADR-0039)

- **Public API** `/v{n}/...`: the only consumer is our module, through the edge gateway (`/api/{experience}/v{n}/**`, prefix removed).
  Breaking change = new `/v{n+1}`; the previous version stays until it is retired.
- **Internal API** `/internal/v{n}/...`: consumers are BFFs of other experiences, in the cluster only, never routed by the gateway.
  Operations are designed for the consumer (e.g. a widget), not as generic domain access. Changes are backward compatible only; a
  breaking change is a new version with an agreed end of the old one. Every controller is protected with
  `[Authorize(Policy = {Experience}BffScopes.X)]`, the policy registered in `Program.cs` with `policy.RequireScope(...)`
  (`ScopePolicyExtensions`), scope `{experience}.internal.{action}`; system calls (no user) would use `{experience}.internal.system.*`
  with the justification in the contract.
- `Hosting/BffOpenApiDocuments.cs` splits the documents by path (`internal/` → internal). The build generates
  `{Experience}.Bff_public.json` and `{Experience}.Bff_internal.json` (OpenAPI 3.0, `operationId` = `{Controller}_{Action}`, Bearer
  security scheme); both are committed and their diff is reviewed. `ContractSplitTests` checks the split.

## Clients of the domain services

- Generated by Refitter from the service's committed contract (`src/Services/{Service}/{Service}.Api/openapi/{Service}.Api.json`),
  settings in `Clients/{Service}/{service}.refitter`: `typeAccessibility: Public` (the types are part of the BFF contract),
  `returnIApiResponse: true`, `useCancellationTokens: true`, `usePolymorphicSerialization: true`,
  `operationNameGenerator: SingleClientFromOperationId`, `operationNameTemplate: {operationName}Async`, output `./Generated`.
- Regenerate after every change of the service contract: `dotnet tool restore`, then
  `dotnet refitter --settings-file src/Bff/{Experience}.Bff/Clients/{Service}/{service}.refitter`. Never edit `Generated/*.cs`; commit
  it with the contract change.
- Register in `Program.cs`: `builder.Services.AddDownstreamApi<I{Service}Api>(builder.Configuration, "{Service}").AddUserTokenForwarding();`
  (Refit, standard resilience with retries only for idempotent methods, ISO dates in URLs). The address `Downstream:{Service}:BaseAddress`
  goes to `appsettings.json` (cluster Service address), `appsettings.Development.json` (`http://localhost:51xx`), the BFF container in
  `deploy/local/docker-compose.yml` (`Downstream__{Service}__BaseAddress`) and the Helm values (`downstream: { {Service}: ... }`).
- Calls are made in the user's context: the user's token is forwarded unchanged (ADR-0040). `IDownstreamTokenProvider` is the seam for
  token exchange; never read or build tokens in BFF code, never log them. Client credentials (`AddClientCredentialsToken`) only for
  system calls, as an explicit exception.

## Actions

- Pass-through action: `this.ToActionResult(await client.XAsync(..., cancellationToken))` (`DownstreamResponseExtensions`); the service's
  status and error body (with `code`) go to the module unchanged. Do not reinterpret or remap service errors.
- Paths: `/v{n}/{service}/...` matching the service's `/v{n}/...` (`/v1/knowledge/materials` → Knowledge `/v1/materials`). Controllers
  `Controllers/{Service}/{Service}{Resource}Controller.cs`, `[Tags("{Service} – {Resource}")]`, request and response types from the
  generated client.
- XML docs of an action repeat the service contract for the module: summary, required scope and rules in `<remarks>`, every
  `<response code>` with its error codes; `[ProducesResponseType]` for every status as in the service.
- No validation in the BFF: `ModelValidatorProviders.Clear()` and `SuppressImplicitRequiredAttributeForNonNullableReferenceTypes` stay on (binding errors such as an unknown enum value still give 400); `ScopeAuthorizationResultHandler` answers policy denials with `403 auth.missing_scope`;
  validation and error codes belong to the services.
- Composed endpoints (several services, e.g. `GET /v1/me/summary`): start the calls in parallel through `PartialResponseFetcher.FetchAsync` (framework, `SuperApp.Framework.Infrastructure.Http.Downstream`)
  (2-second limit per response part), always answer 200 with a `status` per response part (`Ok`, `Forbidden`, `Unavailable`, `Timeout`) and `data`
  only when `Ok` (partial rendering). Cancellation by the client propagates.
- An unreachable or slow service gives `503 downstream.unavailable` / `504 downstream.timeout` (`DownstreamUnavailableExceptionHandler`,
  EventId 220); keep `app.UseExceptionHandler()` and `app.UseStatusCodePages()` (every error has `code` and `traceId`, ADR-0044).
- Logging: `InternalApiCallAudit` (framework global MVC filter, `options.Filters.Add<InternalApiCallAudit>()`) logs every internal API
  call with the route template and the caller's `azp` (EventId 230). Own logs of a BFF use its EventId range from
  `docs/logowanie-eventid.md` (Example.Bff: 6000–6999, e.g. 6001 for a response part that is not `Ok`); never log tokens or user data.

## Gateway, network, deployment

- The gateway routes only `/api/{experience}/v{n}/**` to the BFF's public API; never add gateway routes to domain services or to
  `internal` paths (ADR-0037, ADR-0039). Who may connect to the BFF and the services is decided by NetworkPolicy (ADR-0041); locally
  docker compose does not enforce it.
- The BFF validates the JWT itself (`AddAppApi`, audience `{experience}-bff`), like every service. It may check permissions early for UX,
  but the domain service always checks scope and resource rules.
- Helm: `deploy/helm/superapp-bff` with `values-{experience}.yaml` (`experience` is required, `secretName`, `downstream`); the chart sets the
  labels `app.kubernetes.io/part-of: {experience}` and `superapp.example/experience-role: bff`.

## Tests

- `{Experience}.Bff.Tests`: contract split and security (`ContractSplitTests`), relaying of answers (`DownstreamResponseTests`), generated
  clients with the framework settings (`DownstreamClientTests`), token forwarding, partial rendering (`PartialResponseFetcherTests`). No
  Testcontainers: services are replaced by a recording HTTP handler or by Refit answers built in the test (`Responses`). End-to-end checks go through the local gateway
  (`https://localhost:5001/api/{experience}/v1/...`).
